endpoints.description: The session's conversation, state and delivery progress, with lookup_requirements for explaining requirement IDs.
Answers the questions of the last assistant message and starts a turn.

Resumes the paused coding agent of the named stage workflow. The web client shows each agent's open questions (agent_questions) in the panel's left column, in one form with the interviewer's open questions, and sends each group separately: the interviewer's answers to POST .../answers and each agent's answers here, one call per agent. Agent groups are ordered by stage: implementation, diagnosis, tests, then documentation.

Clears the open-findings flag, keeps the pushed delivery as it is and records findings_acceptance (when and by whom) in the delivery progress. The publication stays marked as unverified. Also allowed after the pull request was merged or closed; the unresolved findings marker (unresolved_findings in GET /workflows) then disappears from both the delivery and its task flow. 409 while no flag is raised.

endpoints.description: Starts a fix round from the instructions, then verification and code review. While the delivery's pull request is open, the result is pushed to the same branch. The instructions are recorded on the review round they start. If verification fails for good, verification_status becomes error, the branch keeps the earlier unverified push and the flag stays raised. Once the pull request was merged or closed (the flow completed or was cancelled), the fix round runs as the delivery child of a new top-level task flow named after the original with a " (fix)" suffix, which links to the original task's stages; its ID is appended to fix_flow_ids, and its result is pushed to a new branch with a new pull request. 409 while no flag is raised.

Starts a new session with the conversation up to the given message, in a new top-level task flow of its own (task_flow_id) named after the original with a " (fork)" suffix, which links to the original task's requirements and architecture sessions and holds a pending delivery child; the original task flow and its children are left unchanged. 409 when the session's flow has completed or been cancelled.

Starts the named stage of the delivery over. The review stage runs a failed code review again; 409 when the delivery has no failed review. The repository stage pushes again and then opens or updates the pull request, which also recovers a pull request step that ended in error; it has the LLM write the pull request's title and description again, and is also allowed when only pull_request_text_error is set (the generic text was used). 409 for the repository stage when there is no publication error, pull request error or pull request text error.

The architecture document as a file attachment: format md (the default) returns architecture.md with its fixed headings, format json returns its machine-readable form, architecture.json, as written to contracts/architecture.json. 404 until it is ready or when the stage was skipped; 422 for any other format.

Skips the stage of an API change, confirming the open skip proposal or, without one, at the user's own request (also after a declined proposal or once a draft exists, which is then discarded). The session ends as skipped and is listed by GET /workflows with status skipped, the repository's existing contracts/architecture.md (and contracts/architecture.json) are kept unchanged and are the architecture given to the API design and coding agents, and the task flow starts its pending API design child (api_design_session_id). 409 for a new service, while drafting or a turn is running, or once the session is finalized, skipped or failed.

Saves the app after GitHub confirms its key and installation, with its optional webhook secret stored encrypted. This is the only way to add or change the webhook secret: connect again with the key and the new secret; leaving it out saves the connection without one. Connecting also fills in webhook_events_missing from the app's subscribed events and the installation's pull_requests permission. The request must be application/json and come from an allowed origin, if any.
Removes the shared connection. The body is an empty JSON object.

Validates the saved app against GitHub and picks up its installation. The body is an empty JSON object. For an app created from the manifest without a webhook secret (created before mentions were supported), it also turns on the app's webhook pointing at POST /connectors/github/events with a newly generated secret, stored encrypted, through GitHub's app webhook configuration. GitHub's API cannot change an app's event subscriptions or permissions, so for every connection, manifest-created or manual, the check reads the app's subscribed events and the installation's permissions and sets webhook_events_missing when issue_comment or pull_request_review_comment is missing or pull_requests: write is not granted; the app's owner must then fix this in GitHub's app settings and check again. A manually connected app keeps its webhook settings; its secret changes only by connecting again.

Saves the app GitHub created from this instance's manifest, with the webhook secret GitHub returns stored encrypted. The manifest turns on the webhook pointing at POST /connectors/github/events and subscribes to issue_comment and pull_request_review_comment events. Connecting also fills in webhook_events_missing from the app's subscribed events and the installation's pull_requests permission.

No sign-in required; called by GitHub. Accepted only when X-Hub-Signature-256 matches the connection's webhook secret, computed over the raw body. A comment mentions the app when it contains @<app slug> or @<app slug>[bot], case-insensitive, as a whole word. Answers 202 with no body when the delivery was accepted and is acted on: a newly created comment (action created) mentioning the app in an issue_comment or pull_request_review_comment event on a pull request the app opened for a delivery or an onboarding, open, merged or closed, by an author with write access, which is then classified and handled; mentions on an onboarding's pull request are handled exactly like those on a delivery's and shown in the onboarding's delivery progress. A clarification or an unclear mention is answered in the pull request right away from the code as last pushed, the same on a merged or closed pull request as on an open one, even while a fix round of the delivery is running or queued. A fix request on a merged or closed pull request (whose delivery has completed or been cancelled) still runs a fix round, followed by verification and code review, as the delivery child of a new top-level task flow named after the original with a " (fix)" suffix and the original's origin, linking to the original task's stages, for a task and for an onboarding alike. Its ID is appended to the original delivery progress's fix_flow_ids and recorded as the mention's fix_flow_id, its result is pushed to a new branch with a new pull request, and the app replies on the old pull request with a link to the new one. Answers 204 with no body when a correctly signed delivery is ignored: other events, edited or deleted comments, and mentions that are not authorised or not on the app's pull requests. Ignored mentions are only logged on the server and not shown in any delivery. Fix requests already queued when the pull request is closed or merged still run. Answers 401 without acting on it when the delivery is unsigned or wrongly signed, or while the connection has no webhook secret. Answers 409 when the delivery (the same X-GitHub-Delivery) or its comment was already handled, such as a GitHub redelivery.

parameters.name: X-Hub-Signature-256

Starts a new top-level task flow (TaskWorkflow with origin onboarding, its ID returned as task_flow_id) on the repository and branch, outside requirements sessions and the intake, which starts the onboarding interview as its child and creates its requirements review and delivery children up front as pending. Any signed-in user can start one, and every signed-in user can list (GET /workflows?origin=onboarding) and reopen all onboardings. When the branch already has a contract in contracts/, contract tests in contract-tests/ or a root Dockerfile, the onboarding waits as awaiting_confirmation, with existing_artifacts saying which were found and architecture_missing whether the contract lacks contracts/architecture.md or contracts/architecture.json, until the user decides through POST /onboarding/sessions/{session_id}/contract-decision; otherwise the LLM drafts the requirements, the architecture, the API and the language from the existing code, all reviewed in the same interview. 409 while another onboarding of the same repository and branch is unfinished.
The onboarding's drafts, conversation, state and delivery progress, with lookup_requirements for explaining requirement IDs.

Answers the questions of the last assistant message and starts a turn. When the requirements review of the drafted requirements reports contradictions (review.status contradictions_found), its questions arrive as one assistant message with one question per contradiction, in the order of review.contradictions. Answering them through this endpoint, one answer per question in that order, records the answers, and the review then runs its next round with the diff of the requirements since its previous round and the questions with their answers (review.status running, onboarding status finalizing). Once a free message has dropped the contradiction questions, they can no longer be answered here. 409 while a review round is running.

Checks the onboarding's branch out again at its latest commit, which the interview reads from the next turn on and the onboarding is finalized against from then on; the onboarding is preparing until it is. The drafts stay as they are. existing_artifacts is refreshed from the new commit; when it now lists a contract, contract tests or a root Dockerfile that were not there before, the onboarding waits as awaiting_confirmation again until POST /onboarding/sessions/{session_id}/contract-decision. A failed update keeps the earlier checkout and says so in error. Refused with 409 while a message is unanswered, a turn or drafting is running, or once the onboarding is finalized, declined or superseded.

replace starts drafting the full contract at the start, or returns to the interview with the drafts kept after a checkout update, and the onboarding then replaces every artifact listed in existing_artifacts (contract, contract tests, root Dockerfile). decline always ends the onboarding as declined, also after a checkout update, which ends its interview and drafts too, and leaves the existing files unchanged. architecture_only drafts only contracts/architecture.md and contracts/architecture.json from the existing code for review in the interview (replacing whichever of the two exists) and leaves every other existing file unchanged; the rest of the existing contract (requirements.json, requirements.md, api.json, openapi.yaml, language.json) must be readable, otherwise 409 with a detail naming the unreadable file, and while the onboarding runs, anything in the drafted architecture that disagrees with api.json or requirements.json is listed in problems, which must be settled in the interview before finalizing. 409 when architecture_missing is false. 409 unless the onboarding is awaiting_confirmation.
endpoints.summary: Decide whether to replace the existing contract

endpoints.description: Resumes the paused coding agent of the named stage workflow, including an agent asking whether a failing contract test reveals a bug in the existing code, which the web client shows in the left column of the onboarding's panel like other agent questions. Like other agent questions, the agent waits for the answer without a timeout. The code is changed only when the answer confirms the bug; otherwise the tests and drafted contract are repaired. A result whose existing code was changed is verified as usual once the tests pass, and its commit message and pull request description say that the existing code was changed. The web client shows agent questions in one form with the interviewer's open questions and sends each group separately, one call per agent here. Agent groups are ordered by stage: implementation, diagnosis, tests, then documentation.

As for a delivery: clears the open-findings flag and records findings_acceptance; the publication stays unverified. Also allowed after the pull request was merged or closed, which clears the unresolved findings marker in GET /workflows. 409 while no flag is raised.

endpoints.description: As for a delivery: starts a fix round from the instructions, then verification and code review, pushing to the same branch while the pull request is open. Once the pull request was merged or closed, the fix round runs as the delivery child of a new top-level task flow (origin onboarding) named after the original with a " (fix)" suffix, which links to the original onboarding task's stages; its ID is appended to the delivery progress's fix_flow_ids, and its result is pushed to a new branch with a new pull request. 409 while no flag is raised.

endpoints.description: For an onboarding that produces the full contract, first starts the task flow's pending requirements review child (review.status running), which checks the drafted requirements against each other and, when the onboarding replaces an existing contract, against that contract's requirements; each contradiction found is asked in the interview as a question, and after the answers the review runs again knowing what changed, without a limit on rounds. After a free message dropped the open contradiction questions (review.status contradictions_found with questions_open false), calling it again starts the next round, given the diff of the drafted requirements since the previous round and the dropped questions marked unanswered. After a failed round (review.status failed), calling it starts a new round on the current drafts, including any changes made by messages since the failure, given the diff since the last finished round; POST .../review/retry instead reruns the failed round with its original input. Only once a round finds no contradictions, or with force=true, are the reviewed drafts fixed as the contract, including contracts/architecture.md, and handed to the task flow, which starts its pending delivery child: contract tests and a root Dockerfile are written and verified against the existing code, then code review, push to a new branch named onboarding/<source branch>-<short id> (the short id taken from the onboarding's session ID) and a pull request to the default branch, as for a delivery. Without force=true, calling it while a round is running or while the contradiction questions are open (questions_open true) answers 409. For an architecture-only onboarding no review runs (its review child closes as skipped), and only contracts/architecture.md (and contracts/architecture.json) is pushed to that branch with a pull request to the default branch, without contract tests, verification or code review; the rest of the existing contract is left unchanged, and disagreements between the drafted architecture and the existing api.json or requirements.json are among the problems that block finalizing. 409 while problems remain or a turn is running.

parameters.description: true to continue despite the requirements review: proceeds at once whatever the review's state (a running round is cancelled, a review not run yet closes as continued anyway with no contradictions) and lists the last finished round's remaining contradictions in the requirements document. false by default.
parameters.name: force

endpoints.description: Starts a new onboarding of the same repository and branch with the conversation, drafts, contract decision and requirements review state (status, round and contradictions) up to the given message, in a new top-level task flow of its own (TaskWorkflow with origin onboarding, returned as task_flow_id) named after the original with a " (fork)" suffix, which holds the forked interview and pending requirements review and delivery children; the review continues from the copied round. Only an unfinished onboarding can be forked: 409 when it is completed, failed, declined or superseded. Forking ends the original as superseded and cancels its task flow with its pending children, so that only the fork stays unfinished and the one-at-a-time rule of POST /onboarding/sessions holds.
Starts the named stage of the onboarding's delivery over, with the same rules as a delivery's stage retry (review and repository stages included).

Starts the interviewer's turn on the user's correction or remark about the drafts. Also allowed while the review's contradiction questions are open (review.status contradictions_found) or after a failed review round (review.status failed). A message sent while contradiction questions are open drops them: review.questions_open becomes false, review.status stays contradictions_found with the last round's contradictions still listed, the questions are no longer answerable through POST .../answers, and the message may change the drafted requirements. Finalizing again starts the next round, given those changes in the diff and the dropped questions marked unanswered. A message sent after a failed round may change the drafted requirements too; review.status stays failed with its error, finalizing again starts a new round on the updated drafts, and POST .../review/retry still reruns the failed round with its original input. The web client warns the user before sending such a message. 409 while a review round is running (review.status running); finalize with force=true stays possible.
Runs the failed drafting or interviewer turn again.
Runs the failed review round of the onboarding's drafted requirements again with the same input (review.status failed); 409 when the last round did not fail.

It creates its other children up front as pending: requirements review, architecture, API design and delivery for a new service or an API change; requirements review and delivery for a bugfix; delivery for a documentation change.

For a new service, API change or bugfix, starts the task flow's pending requirements review child (review.status running) instead of writing the document; each contradiction found is asked in the interview as a question, and once all are answered the review runs again with the diff of the requirements and the answers, without a limit on rounds. After a free message dropped the open contradiction questions (review.status contradictions_found with questions_open false), calling it again starts the next round, given the diff of the requirements since the previous round and the dropped questions marked unanswered. After a failed round (review.status failed), calling it starts a new round on the current requirements, including any changes made by messages since the failure, given the diff since the last finished round; POST .../review/retry instead reruns the failed round with its original input. The document is written, and the session completed, only once a round finds no contradictions or the user finalizes with force=true. Without force=true, calling it while a round is running or while the contradiction questions are open (questions_open true) answers 409. A documentation task writes the document at once, as before, and its review is not created. Once the document is written the task flow's name is rewritten by the LLM from the finalized requirements, and the task flow starts its next pending child: the architecture (architecture_session_id) of a new service or an API change on a repository, or the delivery of a bugfix or documentation task. An API change, bugfix or documentation task is specified against the repository's contract in contracts/, which must include contracts/architecture.md and contracts/architecture.json; 409 when the contract is missing or unreadable, including when either architecture file is missing. The coding agents of a bugfix or documentation delivery receive the repository's existing contracts/architecture.md and contracts/architecture.json read-only, as context, and never change them. When the document is written because the session was idle for a day, no review runs and the task flow's pending children, review included, close as skipped.

endpoints.description: The adapter, model, thinking level and compaction threshold of every LLM workflow type, including the requirements_review entry used by the requirements reviewer of tasks and onboardings, the agent settings, with labels and the selectable models of each provider and their context windows where reported, and the openai_endpoint section shaped by role: base URL, display name and whether an API key is set for the administrator, only the display name for anyone else. The openai adapter is offered in providers only while an endpoint base URL is saved. 503 when a saved key cannot be read without a valid SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY.

Replaces the settings of every LLM workflow type; the body must include requirements_review too (422 otherwise). 422 when a selected model or thinking level is no longer offered, including openai while no endpoint is saved. 422 when a compaction_tokens of a workflow type that is not claude exceeds the context window its provider reports for the selected model. The optional agent section replaces the agent settings; without it they stay unchanged. The optional openai_endpoint section is administrator only: 403 for any other user whose body contains it (also when null), while a body without it saves their workflow settings and leaves the endpoint unchanged. openai_endpoint.base_url must be an http or https URL of at most 2048 characters and display_name at most 100 characters after trimming (422 otherwise). Saving the endpoint with a changed base URL or API key first sends GET {base URL}/models with the new key, or the stored one when api_key is omitted or null, waiting at most 10 seconds; when it does not answer successfully, 422 with a detail giving the HTTP status it answered or the connection error (never the key); 422 also when the base URL changed and no new key was given. A change of the display name alone saves without a check. An empty api_key saves the endpoint without a key. openai_endpoint null removes the endpoint; while any workflow type's saved adapter is openai it answers 409 with an OpenAIEndpointRemovalConflict body (a detail naming those workflow types plus their workflow_types list) and clears nothing; it succeeds without change when no endpoint is saved. The endpoint and the workflow settings are saved in one transaction: any error saves nothing. 503 when a provider's models cannot be listed or SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY is missing. The response has the same shape as GET /settings (SettingsView, with its openai_endpoint section shaped by the caller's role), never the API key; its workflows field holds the saved workflow settings as before.

Newest first, 50 per page. type TaskWorkflow lists only task flows (the top-level flow of each task or onboarding), not RequirementsWorkflow or OnboardingWorkflow executions, which are reached by opening their task flow; type RequirementsWorkflow lists requirements sessions, OnboardingWorkflow onboarding interviews (workflow_id is the onboarding's session_id), RequirementsReviewWorkflow requirements reviews and ArchitectureWorkflow architecture sessions. Every execution also carries repository, branch, name, origin, linked, waiting_for_user and unresolved_findings, each null when it does not apply; the onboarding_id field and filter are removed. The existing fields keep their names and meaning, and status additionally takes the values pending and skipped for stages of a task flow. The optional repository, branch and origin filters combine with type and with each other (all must match); executions whose field is null never match a filter on it, so origin lists only task flows. The repository filter is compared case-insensitively, as on GitHub; the branch filter must match exactly. A malformed filter value (a repository that is not owner/name, an empty branch, or an origin other than requirements or onboarding) answers 422 with a detail, like an invalid type or page_token. Pass the same filters with page_token when continuing. top_level=true lists only executions without a parent: task flows, chats, and the requirements and onboarding flows started before onboardings ran under task flows; no stage of a task (requirements or onboarding interview, requirements review, architecture, API design or delivery, including a delivery started again on its own) is ever top-level. parent=<workflow_id> lists only the direct children of that execution: for a task flow, its requirements (or, for an onboarding's task flow, its onboarding interview), requirements review, architecture, API design and delivery children (including a delivery started again on its own) and, for a forked or fix-round task flow, the original task's earlier stages it links to, with linked true; parent=<a stage's workflow_id> never lists another stage of the task (a requirements, onboarding interview, review or API design session lists none, a delivery its code generation and stage workflows). For a requirements or onboarding flow started before this change, parent lists its children as before. parent and top_level cannot be combined; an empty or malformed parent, or parent with top_level, answers 422.

parameters.name: branch

parameters.description: Only task flows of this origin: requirements (started by a requirements interview) or onboarding (started by an onboarding); 422 for any other value.
parameters.name: origin

parameters.description: Only the direct children of this workflow execution and, for a forked or fix-round task flow, the earlier stages it links to (linked true); 422 when empty or malformed, or combined with top_level.
parameters.name: parent

parameters.description: true lists only executions without a parent workflow: task flows, chats, and the requirements and onboarding flows started before onboardings ran under task flows; a stage of a task is never listed.

properties.description: Set when the user accepted the delivery with its open review findings as it is.
properties.name: findings_acceptance

properties.description: The pull request step after the push, with the same values as publication_status: waiting until the branch is pushed, running while the pull request is opened or updated, completed once it is open or updated, skipped when nothing was pushed, error when it could not be opened or updated (see pull_request_error). An error never fails the push or the delivery; retrying the repository stage pushes again and retries the pull request. Falling back to the generic title and description is not an error: the step still completes (see pull_request_text_error).
properties.name: pull_request_status

properties.description: The pull request opened from the pushed branch to the default branch, once it is open. A later push to the same branch keeps an open pull request and rewrites both its title and its description, and marks a draft ready for review when that push is verified. If the earlier pull request was closed or merged, the later push opens a new one and this field links to it. When updating it fails, this field keeps the existing pull request.
properties.name: pull_request

properties.description: Why the pull request could not be opened or updated, such as the GitHub App installation lacking the pull_requests: write permission, or a network or GitHub API error. Reported the same way whether opening or updating failed. The push and the delivery do not fail because of it; retrying the repository stage tries again. Cleared when the pull request step completes.
properties.name: pull_request_error

properties.description: Why the LLM could not write the pull request's title and description at the last open or update, such as the LLM being unavailable, so the generic text was used instead: today's generic title for the task kind (with the " (unverified)" marker for an unverified delivery) and a generic description made of today's fixed sentence of what the delivery changed, followed only by the open review findings when there are any. The push, the pull request step and the delivery do not fail because of it. While it is set, the repository stage can be retried: it pushes again and has the LLM write the title and description again. Cleared when a later open or update uses LLM-written text.
properties.name: pull_request_text_error

properties.description: Every authorised mention of the GitHub App on the delivery's pull request, oldest first, with its classification and the fix round or reply it led to. properties.description: The workflow_ids of the new top-level task flows started by fix rounds after this delivery's flow completed or was cancelled, oldest first: one per instructions given about its open review findings and per fix request mentioned on its closed or merged pull request. Each is a new TaskWorkflow, with the original's origin and named after the original with a " (fix)" suffix, that holds the fix delivery as its child and links to the original task's stages, for a task's delivery and an onboarding's alike. Empty or absent while none was started.

When the existing code was changed after the user confirmed a bug, the result is still verified as usual once the tests pass, and the pushed commit's message and the pull request's description say that the existing code was changed. schemas.name: ArchitectureDataFlow

properties.description: Name of the component the data comes from.
properties.name: source

properties.description: Name of the component the data goes to.
properties.name: target

properties.description: What data flows and how.
properties.name: description

schemas.description: A key technology choice.
schemas.name: ArchitectureTechnologyChoice

properties.description: What the choice is about, such as storage or messaging.
properties.name: topic

schemas.description: The machine-readable architecture, written to contracts/architecture.json; contracts/architecture.md is rendered from it with fixed headings (Components, Data flow, Technology choices).
schemas.name: ArchitectureStructure

schemas.description: A requirement a requirement ID mentioned in the conversation can refer to, for the web client to show on hover or tap. The list holds one entry per ID and every requirement that applies, without a size limit: when the session records a requirement with the same ID as one of the existing service, the session's version is listed, and an ID the task retires is listed with retired true. For a session without an existing service (a new service, or an onboarding of a branch without a contract), it holds only the requirements recorded or drafted in the session.
schemas.name: LookupRequirement

properties.description: The requirement's ID in canonical form: upper-case prefix, a dash and the number (PREFIX-NUMBER), such as FR-12, whatever form it was recorded in. The client matches fr12, FR12 or fr-12 to it by upper-casing and inserting the dash.
properties.name: id

properties.description: True when the task retires this requirement of the existing service.
properties.name: retired

schemas.description: A contradiction the requirements review found between requirements.
schemas.name: Contradiction

properties.description: Stable ID of the contradiction, C- followed by a number (C-1, C-2, ...), unique across all rounds of the task's review. A contradiction the reviewer reports again in a later round keeps its ID; a new one gets the next number. The requirements document refers to remaining contradictions by it.
properties.name: id

properties.description: What contradicts what, and why.
properties.name: summary

properties.description: The conflicting requirements, in canonical form (such as FR-12): recorded or drafted in the session, or of the existing service (or, for an onboarding replacing a contract, of that contract) and not retired by the task.
properties.name: requirement_ids

properties.description: The question asked of the user on how to resolve it; all of a round's questions are asked in one assistant message, in the order of the contradictions, and answered through POST .../answers.
properties.name: question

schemas.description: The state of the task's requirements review (RequirementsReviewWorkflow, a child of the task flow). The Flows page shows a review flow by opening its requirements or onboarding session in the panel and reading this field, including the contradictions that remained when the user continued anyway.
schemas.name: RequirementsReview

properties.description: not_started until the session is finalized; running while a round runs; passed when a round found no contradictions; contradictions_found after a round reported contradictions, both while the user answers their questions and after a free message dropped them (see questions_open); failed when the round's LLM call failed for good (see error), handled like contradictions_found with none listed, and kept after free messages until a round runs again (POST .../review/retry reruns the failed round with its original input; POST .../finalize starts a new round on the current requirements, whether or not messages changed them since the failure); continued_anyway once finalized with force=true; skipped for documentation, a requirements session or onboarding whose document was written because it was idle for a day, or an architecture-only onboarding.
properties.name: status

properties.description: The current or last round, numbered from 1; 0 before the first round. Rounds are unlimited. A failed round keeps its number: POST .../review/retry reruns it under the same number, while a new round started by POST .../finalize after the failure gets the next number.
properties.name: round

properties.description: The contradictions the last finished round reported, in the order their questions are asked; still listed after a free message dropped their questions; when continued_anyway, those that remained and are listed in the requirements document. Empty when none.
properties.name: contradictions

properties.description: True while the last round's contradiction questions can be answered through POST .../answers, which then starts the next round. Turns false when a free message drops them; status stays contradictions_found and finalizing again (POST .../finalize) starts the next round, given the diff of the requirements and the dropped questions marked unanswered. False in every other status.
properties.name: questions_open

properties.description: Why the last round failed; the round can be retried with its original input under the same number, a new round with the next number started on the current requirements by finalizing again, or the review forced past. Null otherwise.
properties.name: error

schemas.description: The adapter, model, thinking level and compaction threshold of one LLM workflow type.
schemas.name: ModelSettings

properties.description: 1 to 300 characters, without control characters.
properties.name: model

properties.description: 1 to 100 characters; one the model offers.
properties.name: thinking_level

properties.description: Tokens in use at which the coding agents of Pi and the openai adapter compact their history into a checkpoint: 0 never compacts, otherwise at least 4000 and, when the provider reports the model's context window, at most that window (422 otherwise). Defaults to 48000 when omitted; always present in responses. Not checked or used for claude, which compacts its own context.
properties.name: compaction_tokens

schemas.description: The model settings of every LLM workflow type.
schemas.name: WorkflowSettings

properties.description: ModelSettings by workflow type; must hold exactly every type: chat, requirements, requirements_review (the requirements reviewer of tasks and onboardings, separate from review, the code review), api_design, implementation, test_generation, diagnosis, documentation, review and routing; 422 otherwise.
properties.name: workflows

schemas.description: The settings shared by the agents of every workflow type.
schemas.name: AgentSettings

properties.description: 1000 to 10000000 (422 otherwise); default 32000. Contracts whose embedded form is longer reach coding agents as an index plus read-only files instead of whole.
properties.name: contract_embed_chars

schemas.description: The stored settings with the labels and the selectable models.
schemas.name: SettingsView

properties.description: ModelSettings by workflow type, including requirements_review. A workflow type with no saved adapter defaults to pi while no OpenAI endpoint is saved.
properties.name: workflows

properties.description: The saved agent settings, or their defaults while none are saved.
properties.name: agent

properties.description: Display label by workflow type, such as requirements_review: Requirements review.
properties.name: workflow_labels

properties.description: By adapter: label, models (id, label, thinking_levels and context_window: the context window in tokens, null when the provider does not report it), error and hint. The openai adapter is listed only while an OpenAI endpoint base URL is saved, with the endpoint's display name as its label when one is set.
properties.name: providers

properties.description: The OpenAI endpoint: base URL, display name and api_key_set for the administrator; only the display name for any other user.
properties.name: openai_endpoint

schemas.description: The shared OpenAI endpoint as GET /settings shows it, shaped by the caller's role. Never contains the API key.
schemas.name: OpenAIEndpointView

properties.description: Administrator only: the saved base URL; null when no endpoint is saved. Absent for any other user.
properties.name: base_url

properties.description: The saved display name, shown as the openai provider label in the model pickers; null when none is saved (the client then shows OpenAI). Returned to every signed-in user.
properties.name: display_name

properties.description: Administrator only: whether an API key is stored. Absent for any other user.
properties.name: api_key_set

schemas.description: The OpenAI endpoint to save. When the base URL or API key changes, the service first sends GET {base_url}/models with the key, waiting at most 10 seconds; if it does not answer successfully, the whole PUT answers 422 and nothing is saved.
schemas.name: OpenAIEndpointInput

properties.description: Base URL of the OpenAI-compatible endpoint: an http or https URL of at most 2048 characters; anything else answers 422 before any check is sent.
properties.name: base_url

properties.description: The new API key, stored encrypted and never returned. Omitted or null keeps the stored key, which is allowed only while base_url stays the same (422 otherwise); an empty string saves the endpoint without a key.
properties.name: api_key

properties.description: Optional label shown instead of OpenAI in the model pickers; trimmed, at most 100 characters (422 otherwise). Empty, null or omitted saves no display name (null), and the pickers then show OpenAI. Changing only the display name saves without a check.
properties.name: display_name

schemas.description: The body of PUT /settings: the model settings of every LLM workflow type and, optionally, the agent settings and the OpenAI endpoint. Everything is saved in one transaction.
schemas.name: SettingsUpdate

properties.description: ModelSettings by workflow type; must hold exactly every type: chat, requirements, requirements_review, api_design, implementation, test_generation, diagnosis, documentation, review and routing; 422 otherwise.
properties.name: workflows

properties.description: Administrator only (403 for anyone else whenever the key is present, including null). Absent leaves the endpoint unchanged; an object saves it; null removes it (base URL, API key and display name), which answers 409 naming the workflow types whose saved adapter is openai and clears nothing, and is a successful no-op when no endpoint is saved.
properties.name: openai_endpoint

properties.description: Absent leaves the saved agent settings unchanged; an object replaces them.
properties.name: agent

schemas.description: The 409 body of PUT /settings when removing the OpenAI endpoint is blocked because workflow types still use the openai adapter. Nothing is cleared.
schemas.name: OpenAIEndpointRemovalConflict

properties.description: Says the endpoint cannot be removed and names the workflow types whose saved adapter is openai; the Settings page shows it.
properties.name: detail

properties.description: The workflow types whose saved adapter is openai, such as chat or requirements_review, in the order of the workflows keys.
properties.name: workflow_types
